finding.text: Itraconazole inhibited Hedgehog activity in cells and mouse tumors. Human pathway findings are mixed: a prostate study measured skin GLI1 changes, a lung study found no significant GLI1 or PTCH1 change in paired skin samples and no significant decrease in its tumor comparison against unrelated sample sets, and a five-person basal-cell-carcinoma study used sequential arsenic trioxide and itraconazole.

faq.question: Does being an azole mean a drug inhibits Hedgehog signaling or Candida hyphae?
faq.answer: No class-wide conclusion follows. The cited Hedgehog experiments found different responses across azoles, including negative fluconazole and voriconazole reporter results. Candida morphology is a separate in vitro question whose results depended on strain, concentration and exposure. Neither set of observations establishes that an azole treats cancer or improves a patient outcome by this mechanism.
